raw.details:
Welcome to the Hackathon - Project Q - by SRM University - AP!

A team-powered hackathon for building innovative solutions in Software Development.

About the Opportunity:

Hackathon - Project Q is a team participation hackathon in the Software Development category, presented by SRM University - AP. Designed as an coding challenge with a hybrid mode, it gives teams the opportunity to create, refine, and present software solutions through an engaging development journey.

Participants can showcase skills in Project Management, System Testing, Cloud Computing, Quantum Computing, and Software Documentation. From online development to an intensive offline finale, Project Q brings together teamwork, technical execution, and solution-building in a competitive hackathon experience.

Competition Structure

  1. Phase 1 (Online): Track Selection & Prototype Sprint
    • Dates: 8th October – 12th October
    • Deadline: 12th October, 11:59 PM IST
    • Format: Online Development Sprint
    • Details: Teams select a problem statement across 5 specialized domains
      • 1.Quantum Chemistry
              •  Molecular Ground-State Energy (H₂) :- C1
              • Diatomic Potential Energy Surface :- C2
              • Hardware-Efficient H₂O :- C3
              • Open Innovation — Custom Chemistry Problem :- C-OI
      • 2.Quantum Optimization
              •  Max-Cut :- O1
              • Portfolio Selection :- O2
              • Knapsack :- O3
              • Open Innovation — Custom Optimization Problem :- O-OI
      • 3.Quantum Simulation
              • Ising Chain Ground State :- S1
              • Spin Dynamics (Real-Time) :- S2
              • Noise in Trotter Simulation :- S3
              • Open Innovation — Custom Simulation Problem :- S-OI
      • 4.Quantum Machine Learning [QML]
              • Biomedical Signal Classifier :- Q1
              • Quantum Kernel Classifier :- Q2
              • Noise-Resilient Classifier :- Q3
              • Open Innovation — Custom QML Problem :- Q-OI
      • 5.Post-Quantum Cryptography [PQC]
              • Quantum-Safe Secure Channel :- P1
              • Crypto Inventory & Migration Planner :- P2
              • PQC Performance Benchmark :- P3
              • Open Innovation — Custom PQC Problem :- P-OI

    • Important Resources: Access the Problem Statements & Deliverables Drive Link for detailed problem definitions, constraints, submission guidelines, and required deliverables.

    •  https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1caxlXXeqjOkLmXGlimy_Etw0uPHSwyga
    • Deliverables:
      • Submissions require ONE GitHub repository containing an end-to-end implementation (main.ipynb or main.py), setup & execution steps (README.md), processor definitions, and environment files (requirements.txt).
      • You must also include a clear report/analysis with supporting figures and graphs showing an A-versus-B comparison (problem performance, resource usage, and architecture impact).  

2. Phase 2 (Online): Technical Code Audit & Rolling Shortlisting

    • Dates: 12th October – 17th October
    • Format: Online Technical Evaluation
    • Details:
      • Submitted repositories undergo evaluation for code structure, originality, algorithmic design, and reproducibility.
      • Candidate shortlisting is announced on a rolling basis. 

3. Phase 3 (Online): Shortlist Verification & Pass Confirmation

    • Dates: 18th October – 27th October (Confirmation payment window opens on 18th October; final deadline to confirm before 27th October)
    • Format: Virtual Check-in & Spot Confirmation
    • Details:
      • Shortlisted Hackathon Candidates: Must confirm their spot for the finale round by paying the INR 499 Shortlisted Team Pass fee on or before 27th October.
      • Non-Shortlisted Applicants: Can purchase an INR 499 Open Attendee Pass to visit the campus and participate in all parallel events, tech sessions, interactive arenas, and expos (excluding the main hackathon finale).
    4. Phase 4 (Offline): Hackathon Phase 2 — 24-Hour Grand Finale 
    • Dates: 28th October (6:00 PM) – 29th October (6:00 PM)
    • Venue: SRM University-AP Campus
    • Details:
      • 28th Oct (6:00 PM): All instructions, guidelines, and fresh, unreleased problem statements will be revealed live at the venue; the 24-hour continuous hacking clock begins.
      • 29th Oct (10:00 AM): Mid-way mentor and faculty review checkpoint.
      • 29th Oct (4:00 PM – 5:00 PM): Circuit benchmarking, live demonstrations, and formal evaluation.
      • 29th Oct (6:00 PM): Hacking clock stops and final repositories freeze.
       5. Phase 5 (Offline): Winner Announcement - Project Q
    • Date: 30th October
    • Venue: SRM University-AP Campus
    • Details:
      • Following the Grand Finale, the final results, top-performing teams, and Project Q Hackathon winners are officially declared.
      • Awarding Tropies and Cash prize(INR 1,00,000+).
      • Certificates and Special awards are awarded based on jury evaluations.

Rules & Guidelines

    • Eligibility & Teams: 
          • Open to undergraduate, postgraduate, and research scholars.
          • Teams must maintain 2 to 6 members.
          • Inter-institutional teams are permitted.
          • All team members must be registered under this opportunity prior to the Phase 1 submission cut-off.
          • Problem Statements & Development Scope: Online Phase (Phase 1): Solutions must target the initial published problem tracks to qualify for shortlisting.
          • Offline Grand Finale (Phase 4): Teams will receive brand-new, unreleased problem statements on 28th October at 6:00 PM.
          • All development for the offline phase must occur exclusively during the 24-hour on-campus sprint.
          • Code developed prior to the prompt release will not be accepted.
    • Tooling & Platform Access:
        • Permitted frameworks include standard quantum software tool QISKIT and specified hardware backends/simulators.
        • Submissions must include full source code, test execution runs, dependency lists, and documentation.
    • Academic Integrity:
        • All code submitted must be original.
        • Plagiarism, repository scraping, or misattribution will result in immediate team disqualification.
        • Generative AI tools are permitted solely for syntax support, documentation, and troubleshooting; circuit architecture and core algorithms must be implemented by the team.
        • The decisions of the judging committee and organizing panel are final.
